text:
elaine: Thinking out loud — we should extract the rollout/coordinator logic from request-router into a small, independent service. Reasons: clearer ownership, easier canarying, and fewer runtime hot-path churns. Thoughts?

mike: +1 on extraction. Main tradeoff is latency for the hot path if we call the coordinator synchronously. We can cheat with a cached decision in the router for 100ms TTL. :thinking:

priya: Can we make it eventual-consistent? Router reads last-known policy, coordinator pushes updates async. That avoids tail latency but complicates rollout atomicity.

sam: If we go eventual, need strong observability and a safety fallback. E.g., router can fallback to last-stable-model route if decision missing. Also add a "force-fallback" release toggle for incidents.

elaine: Proposed minimal API (HTTP/gRPC): `GET /decision?route=X&model=Y&tenant=Z` returns variant + reasons + decision_id. Router caches by (route,model,tenant) with TTL and decision_id anchor.

mike: Sounds good. Two deployment topologies to evaluate: region-local coordinator (low latency, higher ops) vs central coordinator with replication (simpler code, potential cross-region latency).

priya: For migration, do strangler-style cutover: start with shadowing — router continues to own decisions but logs to coordinator and we compare. After parity, flip read path with canary 1% traffic then 10%.

sam: Agree. Add metrics we'll need: decision_latency, cache_hit_ratio, decision_mismatch_rate (router vs coordinator during shadow), and rollback_count. Also a SLA target: P95 decision time < 5ms for local; < 20ms for central.

elaine: Ownership: runtime team builds coordinator service + test harness. Router team owns cache + fallback. Infra team helps with region deployment patterns.

mike: Data consistency: coordinator should be authoritative for rollouts history and audit logs. Use append-only events in a replicated store (we can use existing config-store). Rollout IDs enable deterministic rollback.

priya: Security: coordinator needs to validate caller identity and tenant scoping. Lock down write APIs to CI/console only.

sam: Runbook notes: 1) If coordinator unavailable and cache cold -> fail open to "stable" variant 2) If decision_mismatch_rate > 0.1% for 5m -> auto-roll back to router-owned decisions 3) Escalate to oncall after rollback_count > 3 in 1h.

elaine: Spike tasks: 1) prototype coordinator in Go + in-memory store (2d) 2) add router shadow logging and comparator (3d) 3) infra: deploy test region-local instance (2d) 4) SME review + security checklist (1d). I'll open tickets.

mike: FYI: infra-bot triggered a canary deploy last hour in staging — looks healthy. infra-bot: deploy staging/rollout-coordinator v0.1 succeeded :shipit:

priya: Small nit: ensure the coordinator API supports bulk decision fetch (batch) to warm the router cache on startup. Saves a ton of cold-start mismatch noise.

sam: Also consider a "sticky decision" mode for long-running sessions to avoid mid-session variant flips. Put that behind a feature flag.

elaine: Great feedback — I'll draft RFC with topology diagrams and migration steps, then link it here for review. Thanks everyone.
